title: Repoint the factory's vitest suite and pin how it gets the fixtures
description:
The TS half. cloud/factory/test/*.test.ts reads the same eight fixtures (tracker-layout.json x4, worker-boot-contract.json x2, sweep-policy-cases.json x2, and one each of the rest) plus omp-tool-call-exchange.json, which is TS-only and stays put — check that assumption rather than moving it by reflex.

Two jobs:
1. Repoint the vitest suite at the new home.
2. Decide and implement HOW ticfac gets these once it is a separate repo. Today a relative path works; after Phase 5 it cannot. The precedent to follow is already in the tree: cloud/sandbox/Dockerfile go-installs tk at a pinned TK_SOURCE_REF from the public module proxy — the image ALREADY consumes ticks as a published, version-pinned artifact. Do the same shape for the contracts rather than inventing a second mechanism.

Options to weigh and choose between, with the reasoning written down: vendor a copy with a sync check in CI; fetch at test time from a pinned ticks ref; publish them as an npm package alongside the existing schemas codegen. The requirement is not elegance — it is that a Go/TS divergence FAILS A BUILD after the repos split. A mechanism that silently no-ops when the fetch fails is worse than a relative path.

Whatever you choose must work TODAY in one repo and CONTINUE to work after Phase 5. Say explicitly what Phase 5 will have to do to it, so 5hm inherits the answer rather than rediscovering it.
acceptance_criteria: The vitest suite reads the fixtures from the new home and passes. The chosen distribution mechanism is implemented and documented, works in-repo today, and is stated to work post-split with what Phase 5 must do written down. A fetch or sync failure FAILS rather than silently skipping. pnpm typecheck and the factory vitest suite green; go test ./... still green.
